questions.prompt: Enabled Blob encryption scopes tenant-a and tenant-b exist in one account. A new container must require tenant-a for every upload, including uploads from clients that explicitly request tenant-b. Which creation-time configuration enforces this requirement?

options.text: Default scope tenant-a; prevent encryption-scope overrides.
options.explanation: Uploads use tenant-a, and requests for a different scope are rejected. Both the required default and override prevention are necessary for this enforced boundary.

options.text: Default scope tenant-a; allow encryption-scope overrides.
options.explanation: Unspecified uploads use tenant-a, but clients can select tenant-b. That violates the requirement that every accepted upload use tenant-a.

options.text: Default scope tenant-b; prevent encryption-scope overrides.
options.explanation: This enforces a scope boundary, but it enforces tenant-b instead of the required tenant-a.

options.text: Default scope tenant-b; allow encryption-scope overrides.
options.explanation: A client could request tenant-a, but other uploads would use tenant-b. Client choice does not enforce tenant-a for every upload.

questions.prompt: A private blob encrypted with the Microsoft-managed encryption scope reports starts returning 403 after that scope is disabled. The disable action was unintended. The client's existing blob-read authorization and network path still work, and no other configuration changed. Which action restores access to this existing blob?

options.text: Re-enable the existing reports encryption scope.
options.explanation: Reads that depend on a disabled scope fail with 403. Re-enabling that same scope restores its availability for the blob while the unchanged authorization and network prerequisites remain satisfied.

options.text: Regenerate the storage account's authorization keys.
options.explanation: Account keys authorize requests; regenerating them does not change the disabled state of the reports encryption scope.

options.text: Grant the client Storage Blob Data Contributor.
options.explanation: Additional data permissions do not re-enable an encryption scope. The client already has read authorization, so that layer is not the failing dependency.

options.text: Create a new enabled scope with a different name.
options.explanation: Creating another scope does not replace the reports scope used to encrypt this existing blob. Its disabled dependency remains until the required scope is re-enabled.

questions.prompt: Private Azure Blob containers use different encryption scopes for two customers. Clients authenticate with Microsoft Entra OAuth tokens. Which configuration authorizes a customer's blob reads separately from those encryption-key boundaries?

options.text: Assign the customer Storage Blob Data Reader at its container scope.
options.explanation: A blob data-role assignment authorizes the authenticated customer to read that container's data. Encryption scopes select encryption keys rather than granting this data permission.

options.text: Assign the customer Reader at its container scope.
options.explanation: Reader grants control-plane resource visibility, not blob data actions. It does not authorize these OAuth blob reads.

options.text: Assign the customer Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User.
options.explanation: This role grants Key Vault key-metadata and wrap/unwrap operations. It does not grant the customer permission to read blobs from a storage container.

options.text: Set the customer's encryption scope as the container default.
options.explanation: A container default chooses the encryption scope for uploads. It does not assign blob-read authorization to the customer identity.
